sections.subtitle: Request Handling
sections.title: What happens before a request is assigned.

blocks.title: Intake quality check
blocks.subtitle: Message · Context · Contact
blocks.body:
Before assigning a request, we check whether the first message includes enough business context for a useful response instead of a generic reply.
---
Identify the decision owner
Confirm country and preferred language
Capture timeline and urgency
Separate service requests from introductions

blocks.title: Information gap review
blocks.subtitle: Details · Evidence · Risk
blocks.body:
The holding team looks for missing details that would slow the specialist team down, then prepares a cleaner handoff path.
---
List missing documents or figures
Check whether more than one unit is involved
Flag unclear commercial assumptions
Define the first useful follow-up question

blocks.title: Ownership handoff
blocks.subtitle: Owner · Next Step · Follow-up
blocks.body:
Once the request is understandable, it is assigned with a clear owner, practical next step, and enough background to avoid restarting the conversation.
---
Choose the responsible team
Share the request summary
Set the first response direction
Keep group-level visibility when needed

sections.subtitle: Working Flow
sections.title: How we move a request from message to next step.

blocks.title: Receive the request
blocks.body: We start with the visitor's message, service area, country, timeline, and preferred follow-up language.

blocks.title: Clarify the context
blocks.body: The holding team checks what information is missing and whether the request is simple, specialist, or multi-unit.

blocks.title: Choose the owner
blocks.body: The request is assigned to the platform that owns the service category and can respond with practical next steps.

blocks.title: Continue with specialists
blocks.body: The specialist team takes over with the right document list, commercial context, quotation path, or coordination workflow.

blocks.title: Keep follow-up clear
blocks.body: The conversation continues with one responsible path, while the holding stays available when more than one unit is involved.

blocks.title: Clear Intake
blocks.body: Every request starts with enough context to understand the goal, market, documents, timeline, and preferred communication path.

blocks.title: Responsible Routing
blocks.body: The holding team avoids vague handoffs by assigning each inquiry to the team that owns the service category.

blocks.title: Specialist Follow-Up
blocks.body: After routing, the relevant platform continues with service-specific questions, evidence, quotation details, or document steps.

blocks.title: Multi-Unit Coordination
blocks.body: When one request touches more than one platform, the holding keeps the conversation organized instead of splitting responsibility.
